你是一位资深对冲基金分析师。读这条信息，是为了检验和形成观点：把支持或削弱已有观点的话和数挑出来，作为证据连到那条观点上；已有观点管不到的，写成候选观点，当场写全：问题、梯子、到期日，带上提出它的证据。

开哪些观点，按材料里能核对的东西定，不凭感觉：
- 数字观点，三种，各开一条：
  1. 这家公司的全年总收入，和它最大那个分部的全年收入。没给全年指引也开，梯子按材料里的实际数和增速划区间。
  2. 材料里公司对今年或明年财年给了全年指引、目标或明确预期的每一个数（毛利率、某个分部或产品线的收入、营业费用、资本开支……）。中间一格放公司给的那个数。
  3. 材料里给出了数字、但不是这家公司自己的事（客户的资本开支、行业的规模、政策的额度），写成主题观点。
  问题写成「〈推动或压住这个数的原因〉能否让〈这个数〉达到〈区间〉？」，比如「AI 基础设施投资能否推动 FY2027 数据中心收入超过 3000 亿美元？」，不写「会达到哪一档」；梯子用这个数的区间。
- 是/否的观点（看一件事）：材料里公司或官方给了日期或期限的待决事项（产品量产或发布的时间、许可或审批、交易完成、法规生效），各开一条，梯子只有「是」「否」两格，到期日就是那个日期。只开结果会动这家公司全年数字或某个分部的事：旗舰产品的量产、大客户的部署、许可和关税；游戏、软件功能、工具和驱动的更新、促销、单款外设不开，当证据连到相关观点上。待决的监管决定（出口许可、审批、关税）没有日期也开，到期日写到当前财年末。kind 仍按讲的是这家公司还是世界写「对象观点」或「主题观点」，没有别的 kind。
- 不开：季度数和季度指引（是证据，连到全年那条上）；超出明年的数；没有日期的话题（护城河、竞争格局、战略方向，当证据连到相关观点上）；高管任免、股东投票和章程细则、例行诉讼程序、回购授权。
- 已有观点里已经有的，不再写候选观点，证据连到已有的那条上；同一件事只写一条。

写观点的规矩：
- 一个观点只看一件东西：一个数（写明哪一年）或一件事。既要数字又要事件的，拆成两条。
- 问题写成一句问句，不写成断言；到期那天有一个数或一件事能判对错。
- 问的是一家公司的收入、利润、份额、产品进度，就是对象观点，object 写这家公司的股票代码，哪怕背后的原因是政策或宏观；主题观点只问世界会变成什么样（许可发不发、利率到哪、资本开支多少），不问某家公司因此怎样。
- 问题、看的是什么、梯子每一格的条件、一句话说清（one_line）都用中文写；原句（quote）照抄原文，不翻译。
- 梯子每一格的条件现在就要写得出具体的数或状态；条件要靠将来才公布的目标值、门槛值的，核对不了，不开。
- 梯子五格（只有是或否的问题两格）。对象观点（公司）的五格从「强烈看多」到「强烈看空」，说的是对这家公司业务好还是坏；主题观点（宏观、政策、行业）的五格是从一头排到另一头的五种结果，用结果命名，不说好坏。每一格是一个能核对的结果：一个数落在哪段区间，或一件事到了哪一步；格和格不重叠、不留空，到期时正好一格成立；中性那一格跟什么比写在条件里；没有含糊的「部分」。
- 到期日定在这个争论见分晓的那天。数字的观点，到期日就是这个数公布的那天；公司的数按它的财年，发布日所在的财年是今年、下一个财年是明年；不是公司的数按自然年。事件的观点写清到哪一天看它处在哪一格。

写证据的规矩：
- 一条证据是信息里的一句原话或一个数，原文照抄（quote），不改一个字；另写一句离开原文也看得懂的话（one_line）：谁、做了什么、多少、哪一期。
- 每条证据写明谁说的（speaker），转述的写明最初是谁、哪天说的（original_who、original_day）；tier 只写这四个词之一：发生的事、当事人说的、第三方看法、传闻。发生的事指官方行动、公布的数、完成的交易；当事人说的指公司指引、管理层表态、官员讲话；第三方看法指卖方、媒体分析、专家；传闻指「知情人士称」和没有出处的说法。
- 每条证据连到它直接讲的那条观点上（links 写观点编号），可以连几条；已有观点管不到的，连到这次的候选观点上（写候选观点的编号）。一句话只连它直接讲的那条，不连间接相关的。没有观点可连的话不抽。
- 背景、套话、广告、导航文字不抽。
- 只凭这条信息写，不用你自己知道的别的事。

每个候选观点另填一把键，让代码判断两条观点是不是同一个量：
- measure：从清单里选最贴的量。公司的数：total_revenue、segment_revenue、product_revenue、gross_margin、operating_margin、operating_expense_growth、total_expenses、operating_loss、tax_rate、capex、shipments_or_capacity、run_rate、design_wins；事件：event；世界的数：spend_total、financing_amount、price、capacity、growth_rate、policy_event；都不是：other。
- scope：量的实际限定范围；分部、产品、群体或事件对象。参考名称含义相同时沿用，没有限定写空字符串。
- period_start / period_end：这个量覆盖的起止日（ISO）。财年按财年说明换算；自然年 2026 = 2026-01-01 到 2026-12-31；事件写提出当年年初到到期日。
- basis：GAAP、non_GAAP 或 n/a。unit：USD、percent、count、GW、MW、TWD、multiple 或 n/a。event_type：measure 是 event 或 policy_event 时选 launch、shipment、licence、approval、deal_close、deployment、other，否则 n/a。
- 梯子每格另写 lo、hi：这一格数值区间的下界（含）和上界（不含），用 unit 的单位（美元写完整数字，百分比写 73 不写 0.73）；最低格 lo 写 null，最高格 hi 写 null；是/否两格都写 null。

【这一类是什么、怎么读】T8。观点与分析：卖方、独立研究、评论、个人帖子。作者的看法和估计都是第三方看法，不是发生的事；作者引用的公司原话算当事人说的。

【讲的是谁】这条信息的相关对象：NVDA。候选观点讲的是公司时，object 写股票代码；讲的是主题时，从下面名单里挑一个写编号，名单里没有的写清是什么事：
  - chip-export-controls：芯片出口管制
  - ai-capex：AI 资本开支
  - custom-silicon：云厂商自研芯片
  - semiconductor-cycle：半导体周期
  - fed-policy-rate：美联储政策利率
  - us-inflation：美国通胀
  - us-recession-risk：美国衰退风险
  - us-china-tariffs：中美关税
  - taiwan-strait：台海局势
  - middle-east-conflict：中东冲突与油价
  - russia-ukraine-war：俄乌战争
  - supply-chain-shift：供应链转移与航运
财年说明（数字观点的年份和到期日按这个算）：
NVDA 的财年在 1 月结束，财年按结束的那一年命名：FY2027 从 2026-02 到 2027-01，发布日 2026-07-27 落在 FY2027，所以今年是 FY2027，明年是 FY2028；FY2027 的全年数在 2027-02 前后的年报里公布，到期日按那天写。

【这一类要读出什么】作者的看法、论据、预测、评级和目标价，以及它们的变化；作者引用的事实和数字（注明出处）。

【研究参考】已有的量和范围（measure[scope](event_type)）。含义相同可用现有名称；清单外的重要问题照常提出，保留实际范围：
  - NVDA：total_revenue；segment_revenue；gross_margin；operating_margin；operating_expense_growth；tax_rate；capex；product_revenue[Blackwell+Rubin]；product_revenue[Vera]；shipments_or_capacity[Rubin]；event[Rubin](shipment)；event[Rubin](launch)；event[H20/H200 China](licence)；event[SK Telecom AI factory](deployment)

【这些对象已有的观点】还没有。该开的都写成候选观点。

Nvidia's potential new deal with OpenAI would revive a spooky tech-bubble habit, analyst warns
Nvidia's potential new deal with OpenAI would revive a spooky tech-bubble habit, analyst warns
Provided by Dow Jones
Jul 28, 2026, 2:46:00 AM
By Hannah Pedone
Investors are fretting over a report that Nvidia could backstop an OpenAI data-center lease, in what would be the largest such arrangement yet
Nvidia is in talks to provide a $250 billion backstop that would allow OpenAI to lease an Ohio data center, according to the Wall Street Journal.
As investors question the value of heavy artificial-intelligence spending, the specter of vendor financing once again hangs over the technology sector.
On Sunday, the Wall Street Journal reported that Nvidia (NVDA) is in talks to guarantee $250 billion in financing that would allow OpenAI to lease a data center being built in Ohio. The Ohio facility could cost over $500 billion and would be the largest data-center project announced to date, according to the Journal.
Nvidia and OpenAI did not respond to requests for comment.
Even though it remains to be seen how a hypothetical deal would be structured, Seaport Research's Jay Goldberg is cautious on this sort of arrangement.
"I don't know all the details or even how real this is, but if it does happen, I think it's hard to justify for Nvidia," he said.
Goldberg noted that companies have previously "tripped themselves up with financing customer purchases." He cited the telecom company Lucent, which engaged in vendor financing to boost sales in the 1990s. The decision "essentially broke that company," he told MarketWatch.
"These kinds of financing usually don't end well," Goldberg added.
Shares of Nvidia lost 5% in Monday's trading.
The Nvidia-OpenAI deal looks even more unusual when considering the electricity required to power the Ohio data center. The project is located on a decommissioned uranium-enrichment site, and the campus would require 10 gigawatts of electricity.
In exchange for lower tariffs, Japan has agreed to invest $33 billion in a natural-gas power project that will be operated by data-center developer SB Energy, a subsidiary of SoftBank Group (JP:9984) (SFTBY). OpenAI is also an investor in SB Energy.
The backing by Nvidia would enable SoftBank to raise debt on more favorable terms - which would otherwise be challenging given how S&P Global has flagged OpenAI as a key credit risk.
The U.S. government will pay a fee to SB Energy to operate the plant, but the revenue will be divided between Japan and the U.S. - that is, until Japan has been repaid its $33 billion. From that point, the U.S. would keep 90% of the revenue, which would come from OpenAI, a future buyer of the energy.
The Trump administration has pitched the deal as a win for Americans and Ohio, despite growing pushback against the data-center buildout.
Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said in a March post on X that the project was "only made possible by President Trump's trade and tariff policy!!" He added that it promises to "create thousands of jobs, lower electricity costs for American families, and deliver energy infrastructure needed to power the AI economy."
The project is located on federal land in southern Ohio.
The deal would be the latest in a string of vendor financing agreements in the AI ecosystem, whereby a seller lends to a buyer of its products.
"Investor feedback late last night was a combination of this being the clearest/largest circular-financing headline we've seen so far and we're not entirely new to this circular-financing debacle," Jefferies technology strategist Jeffrey Favuzza said in a note to clients.
Nvidia already has committed to investments in OpenAI, and also amended some of the earlier terms of such arrangements. In February, the Financial Times reported that Nvidia was pulling out from a $100 billion agreement originally announced in September, and replacing it with a $30 billion equity investment.
Broadcom (AVGO) and Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) also have partnerships with OpenAI to deploy their chips. Additionally, OpenAI has committed $300 billion to Oracle (ORCL) to secure data-center capacity, much of which Oracle will use to buy Nvidia GPUs. Meanwhile, Nvidia holds $2 billion in cloud provider CoreWeave's stock (CRWV).
See also: Nvidia's Jensen Huang has a high-stakes message for AI policymakers
-Hannah Pedone
